final_candidates.decision_summary: Zinc-coordinating RING cysteine with the highest pathogenicity score (z=0.990); loss of this ligand is a classic, well-established mechanism for abolishing BRCA1 RING/E3 function while a single substitution preserves global fold.
Highest AlphaMissense score in the pool (z=0.992); proline at this conserved RING core position should disrupt local secondary structure and destabilize the functional RING domain.
Second zinc-ligand cysteine with z=0.988; removing zinc coordination collapses the RING fold locally and abolishes tumor-suppressor E3 ligase activity.

stop_reason.detail: Phenotype evidence is strong, convergent, and the remaining tools are either non-informative or not applicable, so additional rounds would not alter the Top-3.

history.rationale: Cys61 in the RING domain zinc finger coordinates Zn2+; loss disrupts E3 ligase activity and BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer function, a classic pathogenic LOF variant. Local backbone stays globular.
C61 is a zinc-coordinating Cys in the BRCA1 RING domain (C3HC4); mutation destroys RING folding/E3 ligase function, a classic LOF mechanism.
Highest-tier AlphaMissense (0.990) and known RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; disrupts BARD1 binding and E3 function.

Highest-priority zinc-coordinating RING cysteine; top AlphaMissense (0.990) and near-absent mutant frequency (0.036) confirm disruption of a conserved functional residue, exactly matching the LOF goal.
Cys44 coordinates the second RING zinc; mutation abolishes zinc binding and RING folding/function, a well-documented pathogenic mechanism. Protein remainder remains intact.
C44 is another RING zinc ligand; loss disrupts RING structure and BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer function, known pathogenic class.
AlphaMissense 0.988; zinc-ligand cysteine in RING, classic pathogenic LOF driver.
Zinc-coordinating cysteine with AlphaMissense 0.988; MSA frequency 0.131 slightly higher than C61G but still supports functional constraint.
Ile26 sits in the RING hydrophobic core at the BARD1 interface; mutation destabilizes RING dimerization and E3 activity, known pathogenic LOF variant.
I26 lies in the RING/BARD1 interface; hydrophobic-to-small change may disrupt E3 interaction; lower priority than zinc ligands.
AlphaMissense 0.979 supports strong LOF; retained but RING cysteine variants have stronger mechanistic priors.
Strong AlphaMissense (0.979) in conserved RING core; good fallback but conservative Ile->Ala change is less certain to abolish function than cysteine losses.
Arg1699 in the first BRCT repeat is critical for phospho-peptide binding; R1699 mutations are established pathogenic LOF alleles disrupting DNA-damage signaling.
R1699 in BRCT-N is a known pathogenic hotspot (R1699W/Q) affecting BRCT stability and phospho-recognition.
AlphaMissense 0.735 is weakest pathogenic score among BRCT candidates; demote.
Weakest AlphaMissense (0.735) among actives and no usable MSA; demote to bottom of pool.
Ser1655 in BRCT1 anchors the phosphopeptide-binding pocket; S1655 substitutions are pathogenic and impair phospho-ligand recognition.
S1655 sits in BRCT-N; conservative substitution, weaker expected LOF — candidate for rejection if evidence favors stronger hits.
AlphaMissense 0.337 (benign class) contradicts LOF goal; remove from active pool.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense 0.337 (benign class) contradicts LOF goal; remove from active pool.

history.rationale: Met1775 in BRCT2 forms a hydrophobic pocket; M1775R is a well-characterized pathogenic variant that disrupts BRCT phospho-ligand binding and transcriptional activation.
M1775R is a well-characterized pathogenic BRCT-domain variant disrupting phosphopeptide binding while retaining fold; strong LOF proxy.
AlphaMissense 0.893; documented BRCT pathogenic variant, but charge introduction may perturb local folding more than desired.
Known BRCT-interface disruptor with AlphaMissense 0.893, but negligible MSA coverage limits corroboration; keep as mid-tier backup.
Gly1788 in BRCT2 lies in a structurally constrained loop; G1788V is a known pathogenic missense causing LOF while the domain largely retains fold.
G1788 in BRCT-C; Gly-to-Val likely perturbs local backbone conformation in the BRCT repeat.
AlphaMissense 0.925 in BRCT phospho-recognition domain; credible LOF but slightly below top tier.
AlphaMissense 0.925 is decent but MSA coverage is only 9/211 homologs (app 0.04), so evolutionary support is uninformative; demote.
Cys27 is a RING zinc-coordinating residue; mutation destroys the RING fold and ubiquitin ligase function, producing LOF.
C27 is a RING zinc-coordinating Cys; mutation abrogates zinc binding and RING function.
AlphaMissense 0.983; third zinc-coordinating RING cysteine, coherent mechanistic class with C61G/C44G.
Third zinc-ligand cysteine with AlphaMissense 0.983; MSA frequency 0.182 somewhat tolerant, keeping it just below the top three.
Leu22 precedes the RING zinc finger; a Pro substitution could distort the RING N-terminal helix and impair function, but risk of local misfolding is higher.
L22P may disrupt RING helix but risks broader misfolding; lowest confidence, likely to be dropped.
Highest AlphaMissense in pool (0.992) — move up from rank 9; proline substitution at RING-domain N-terminus likely distorts domain architecture without global unfolding.
Highest AlphaMissense (0.992) with full MSA coverage and low mutant frequency (0.028); proline substitution likely disrupts RING fold while remaining a single point change.
